brief: What actually makes a team ship fast

slots.sub: They have removed the six places where a decision waits on somebody. Here is each one and what replaced it.

slots.titleLine1: Ship the smallest thing that is
slots.body: Large scope is not ambition, it is deferred learning. Every week between deciding and shipping is a week you are guessing about what people wanted.
slots.tileKey: If it cannot ship this week, it is still too big.

slots.body: Committees do not decide, they schedule. One named person gathering input and choosing is faster and, when it goes wrong, it is fixable.
slots.tileKey: If everyone owns it, nobody does.

slots.titleLine1: Review is a queue, and queues
slots.body: A change waiting a day is not idle, it is rotting. Context leaves the author's head and the review gets slower the longer it sits.
slots.tileKey: Small changes reviewed today beat perfect ones reviewed Friday.

slots.body: The meeting where design explains itself to engineering exists because they worked in sequence. Working in the same file removes the meeting entirely.
slots.tileKey: If it needs explaining, it was built too far from the people building it.

slots.body: Teams re-litigate settled decisions because nobody recorded the reasoning. The record is not bureaucracy, it is the thing that stops the same argument recurring quarterly.
slots.tileKey: If you cannot say why, you will have this discussion again.

slots.body: Every team with these tools still ships slowly if decisions wait on approval. The software makes a good culture faster; it does not make a slow one good.
slots.tileKey: Change who decides before you change what they decide in.

slots.tagline: Not all six. Find the single step where things sit longest this month and remove the wait. Do that repeatedly and it compounds.
